mcp.native: stdlibio and HTTP transports; JSON-RPC 2.0 request_id correlation on stdio; SSE/WS streams carry request_id too. No session-level identity binding in base transport.
mcp.native_field_selector: request_id (JSON-RPC); transport-level (stdio, HTTP+SSE, WebSocket) via MCP-2026-07-28-SPEC

a2a.native: HTTP JSON-RPC and WebSocket transports; each request carries a unique id. No session-level identity binding; caller identity is asserted per-request via authentication field on the Agent Card.
a2a.native_field_selector: id (JSON-RPC request); JSON-RPC-HTTP/WebSocket transport per A2A-1.0.0-SPEC

matrix.hub: Canonical envelope requires correlation_id + causation_id; tenant/workspace/goal/task/run scoping on every request. Correlation is bound to an authenticated principal and a canonical session ledger entry.

adapter_mapping.MCP: Map request_id to correlation_id. If protocol payload carries no causation, derive from prior envelope. Scopes from hub routing, never from protocol payload.
adapter_mapping.A2A: Map request id to correlation_id; Task.id to task_id (hub-issued, not protocol-asserted as authoritative).

matrix.lossiness_note: Protocol request_id is not bound to a hub-authenticated principal. Adapter attaches hub session context; protocol id becomes a secondary reference only.
matrix.security_consequence: Request IDs alone cannot prove request origin or non-replay; hub enforces replay protection separately.
assumptions: MCP/A2A request correlation is a transport concern, not a security boundary.
matrix.owner_followup: None required; this is a transport mapping.

matrix.surface: task lifecycle, cancellation and terminal authority

mcp.native: MCP base protocol has no task abstraction. 2026-07-28 introduces Tasks for async long-running tool operations, but the protocol task lifecycle is internal to the client-server exchange.

a2a.native: Task with TaskState: SUBMITTED, WORKING, INPUT_REQUIRED, COMPLETED, FAILED, CANCELLED, REJECTED, AUTH_REQUIRED, UNIMPLEMENTED, UNKNOWN. cancelTask cancels a task; completed/failed/cancelled/rejected are terminal. The agent server owns terminal authority; the client requests.

matrix.hub: Tasks have a guarded lifecycle with single canonical state owner. Only a Gate evaluation over an evaluator record can ACCEPT a Goal. Cancellation completes the protocol task but does NOT cancel reconciliation side effects.
matrix.hub_semantic: Guarded state machine: DRAFT -> ACTIVE -> ... -> terminal (via reconciliation). Cancellation is a transition, not a reconciliation terminator.

adapter_mapping.MCP: MCP task result is data, not terminal authority for hub task. Hub task reaches terminal only via its own state machine + reconciliation. Adapter DENIES any protocol payload claiming task completion implies effect completion.
adapter_mapping.A2A: Map A2A TaskState to a STATUS_REPORTED event type. Hub terminal state is decided by hub state machine + reconciliation, NOT by A2A TaskState.COMPLETED. If A2A reports COMPLETED but hub reconciliation shows unknown outcome, hub stays in reconciliation.

matrix.lossiness_note: Protocol task state is a report, not a terminal authority. The adapter must not conflate protocol completion with hub terminal acceptance.
matrix.security_consequence: Treating protocol TaskState.COMPLETED as hub terminal would allow protocol payloads to declare completion without reconciliation.
assumptions: Hub task lifecycle is stricter than any protocol task lifecycle.
matrix.owner_followup: S1-008 (revocation latency) defines the reconciliation contract.

mcp.native: tools/call invokes a named tool with arguments, returns CallToolResult. tools/list enumerates available tools. resources/read reads a resource URI. No effect-class attribution (read vs write_local vs dangerous) in the protocol.

a2a.native: Agent Card declares skills. Task execution is opaque to the client. No tool-level effect classification.

matrix.hub: Every tool invocation must pass a ToolGateway with capability check, effect class (read/write_local/dangerous), idempotency key, and approval before execution.
matrix.hub_semantic: Effect class is assigned by the hub from a registry-resolved ToolContract, never by the protocol.

adapter_mapping.MCP: Map MCP tool name to hub ToolContract via registry lookup (NOT the protocol-advertised name directly). Effect class from the registry contract. Protocol-advertised tool list is an untrusted claim; adapter DENIES tools not in the registry.
adapter_mapping.A2A: A2A has no per-tool invocation surface at the protocol level. Skills map to hub capability scope only after registry resolution. Adapter DENIES unrecognized skills.

matrix.lossiness_note: Protocol tool names are not authorization. Registry resolution is required before any effect.
matrix.security_consequence: Accepting protocol-advertised tool names as authorization would allow arbitrary capability escalation.
assumptions: Hub registry is the sole authority for tool effect classification.
matrix.owner_followup: S1-009 adapter contract defines the tool-name-to-contract mapping rules.

mcp.native: MCP 2026-07-28 has no principal identity in the base protocol. Authorization is addressed by a separate MCP Authorization spec (OAuth 2.1). The base protocol carries no authenticated principal claim.
mcp.native_field_selector: No principal identity field in base MCP-2026-07-28-SPEC; MCP Auth extension separate

a2a.native: Agent Card carries an 'authentication' field describing auth requirements, but the card is self-asserted. No principal identity is bound to individual task requests in the core protocol.

matrix.hub: A canonical authenticated actor (principal) is required for all operations. Asserted remote actor is an untrusted claim until registry/policy verifies it. Authenticated actor and asserted remote actor are distinct envelope fields.
matrix.hub_semantic: authenticated_actor (hub-verified) vs asserted_remote_actor (untrusted claim); assertion must be verified before use.

adapter_mapping.MCP: No authenticated principal in base MCP. Adapter sets authenticated_actor from hub session context. asserted_remote_actor stays null/unknown unless hub verifies it. Protocol payload cannot set authenticated_actor.
adapter_mapping.A2A: Agent Card authentication is a capability advertisement, not a principal binding. Adapter sets authenticated_actor from hub transport auth; asserted_remote_actor may be populated from Agent Card contact but must be verified.

matrix.lossiness_note: Protocol does not provide hub-authenticated principal identity. Adapter must leave authenticated_actor unpopulated-by-protocol and rely on hub session binding.
matrix.security_consequence: If adapter trusted protocol-advertised identity, an attacker could impersonate any principal.
assumptions: MCP auth extension and A2A auth schemes are transport-level, not protocol-payload-level.
matrix.owner_followup: Identity federation is non-scope for S1-009 (production identity federation is explicitly excluded).

mcp.native: ServerCapabilities negotiated in InitializeResult; tools/list, resources/list, prompts/list enumerate available endpoints. ClientCapabilities in InitializeRequest. Static capability set per connection.

a2a.native: Agent Card (AgentCard) declares skills, capabilities (streaming, pushNotifications, stateOverflow), and authentication. Discovered via well-known path or getAgentCard.

matrix.hub: Capabilities are registry-resolved contracts with version and exact canonical arguments. Discovery is untrusted claim until registry/policy verification.
matrix.hub_semantic: registry-resolved capability/tool contract ID + version; protocol-advertised capabilities are untrusted claims.

adapter_mapping.MCP: Protocol-advertised tools/resources/prompts are untrusted claims. Adapter resolves each against the hub registry. Unregistered tools are DENIED. Extension capabilities are QUARANTINED unless explicitly accepted.
adapter_mapping.A2A: Agent Card skills and capabilities are untrusted claims. Adapter resolves against hub registry. Unknown skills are DENIED. Advertised pushNotifications/streaming are transport claims, not capability grants.

matrix.lossiness_note: Protocol capability advertisement is a hint, not an authorization. The adapter narrows by registry resolution.
matrix.security_consequence: Trusting advertised capabilities without registry resolution enables Probe B (capability expansion).
assumptions: Hub registry is the source of truth for capabilities.
matrix.owner_followup: S1-010 (tool-poisoning detection) builds on this boundary.

matrix.surface: exact-action delegation grants and child scope

mcp.native_field_selector: No delegation grant, approval, expiry, or child-scope fields in MCP-2026-07-28-SPEC

a2a.native_field_selector: No delegation grant, approval, expiry, or child-scope fields in A2A-1.0.0-SPEC

matrix.hub: Exact-action delegation: grant binds to actor + exact operation + canonical arguments + expiry. One-time use. Consumed atomically. Child scope is a narrowed subset.
matrix.hub_semantic: grant_id, delegator/delegatee, capability_id, arguments_digest, expiry, consumed, fencing_token, revocation_epoch.

adapter_mapping.MCP: Protocol payloads claiming delegation or approval are treated as untrusted text. grant_present remains false. Adapter returns DENY/needs-governance on any effect path that requires a grant. (Probe A)
adapter_mapping.A2A: Same: protocol Task/Artifact text/metadata claiming delegation does not create a grant. grant_present stays false. DENY on effect paths requiring a grant.

matrix.lossiness_note: Delegation is entirely absent from both protocols. Cannot be losslessly translated; must be denied and escalated to hub governance.
matrix.security_consequence: If protocol payload could create grants, an attacker could self-authorize arbitrary actions.
assumptions: Delegation is a hub-only authority surface.
matrix.owner_followup: S1-009-FU-01 (Delegation Grant Contract) — named owner: Gateway/Policy; define exact-action grant, child scope, expiry, atomic consumption, and revocation test before claiming support.

mcp.native_field_selector: No owner principal, fencing token, or revocation epoch fields in MCP-2026-07-28-SPEC

a2a.native_field_selector: Task has no owner principal field; reassignment/cancellation is client-initiated without principal verification in A2A-1.0.0-SPEC

matrix.hub: Owner principal is hub-resolved. Fencing tokens and revocation epochs prevent replay/stale delegation after reassignment. Only the hub can reassign ownership.
matrix.hub_semantic: owner_principal (hub-resolved), fencing_token, revocation_epoch; reassignment creates a new epoch.

adapter_mapping.MCP: No ownership in protocol. Adapter assigns owner from hub session/auth context. Protocol payload cannot set owner.
adapter_mapping.A2A: A2A Task has no owner field. Adapter assigns owner from hub transport auth. Protocol cancelTask is a cancellation request, not an ownership transfer; hub checks fencing/revocation epoch.

matrix.lossiness_note: Protocol does not model ownership. Adapter populates owner from hub context only.
matrix.security_consequence: Allowing protocol payload to set ownership would enable privilege escalation via task hijacking.
assumptions: Hub transport auth is the source of owner identity.
matrix.owner_followup: S1-004 (formal invariant simulation) defines fencing semantics.

mcp.native_field_selector: No budget, quota, or cost fields in MCP-2026-07-28-SPEC

a2a.native_field_selector: No budget, quota, or cost fields in A2A-1.0.0-SPEC

matrix.hub: Budget with currency/unit; parent_total, reserved, consumed, remaining. Child splits, unit mismatches, negative/overflow/missing values, and parallel aggregation cannot increase parent budget. Fail closed on malformed input.
matrix.hub_semantic: budget conservation invariant; reservation <= remaining; consumption <= remaining.

adapter_mapping.MCP: No budget in protocol. Adapter sets budget from hub ledger for the resolved capability/task. Protocol cannot provide budget values. Empty/missing/negative/overflow -> DENY (fail closed). (Probe C)
adapter_mapping.A2A: Same: no budget in protocol. Hub ledger is the sole source. Malformed budget claims from protocol -> DENY.

matrix.lossiness_note: Budget is absent from both protocols. Adapter injects hub-side budget; never accepts protocol-provided budget values.
matrix.security_consequence: Accepting protocol budget values would enable budget laundering (Probe C).
assumptions: Hub budget ledger is the source of truth; protocol carries no budget semantics.
matrix.owner_followup: S1-009-FU-02 (Budget Conservation Contract) — named owner: Scheduler/Budget; specify reservation, consumption, aggregation, unit, overflow, and reconciliation evidence before claiming support.

matrix.surface: idempotency, receipts, unknown outcome and reconciliation

mcp.native_field_selector: No idempotency key or receipt mechanism in base MCP-2026-07-28-SPEC. Request_id provides transport-level dedup within a session but is not an idempotency key for effects.

a2a.native_field_selector: No explicit idempotency key or receipt mechanism in A2A-1.0.0-SPEC. Task ID provides deduplication but not effect-level idempotency.

matrix.hub: Every retriable side effect declares an idempotency key or compensation. Unknown outcomes escalate to reconciliation, never blind retry. Cancellation does not cancel reconciliation.
matrix.hub_semantic: idempotency_key (host-assigned), receipt_state, reconciliation_state with unknown_outcome handling.

adapter_mapping.MCP: Protocol request_id is NOT an idempotency key. Adapter attaches a host-assigned idempotency_key from the canonical ledger. If protocol result is ambiguous (unknown), hub enters reconciliation. Cancellation of MCP task does not resolve reconciliation.
adapter_mapping.A2A: Protocol Task ID is NOT an idempotency key. Adapter attaches host-assigned idempotency_key. Unknown TaskState (UNKNOWN) -> hub reconciliation. cancelTask does not cancel reconciliation.

matrix.lossiness_note: Protocol lacks idempotency/receipt semantics. Adapter injects host-side keys; reconciliation is hub-only.
matrix.security_consequence: Using protocol IDs as idempotency keys allows duplicate or missed effects on retry.
assumptions: Hub canonical ledger is the idempotency authority.
matrix.owner_followup: S1-004 SAF/INV simulations define reconciliation semantics.

mcp.native_field_selector: Tool results may carry arbitrary metadata in CallToolResult; no structured provenance or evidence-linkage fields in MCP-2026-07-28-SPEC

a2a.native_field_selector: Artifacts carry data parts and optional metadata; no structured provenance/evidence-linkage fields in A2A-1.0.0-SPEC

matrix.hub: Every artifact has canonical ref, SHA-256, content length, and provenance. Protocol-native payload digest is recorded (metadata only, never raw secrets).
matrix.hub_semantic: input_artifacts[] and output_artifacts[] with sha256 + provenance; protocol_payload_digest for the non-secret payload.

adapter_mapping.MCP: If protocol result lacks provenance fields, adapter populates from hub ledger (host-assigned provenance). If protocol result CLAIMS provenance it cannot back, adapter marks it untrusted. Loss of required scope/policy/provenance in an accepted mapping -> FAIL.
adapter_mapping.A2A: Same: hub assigns provenance. Protocol artifact metadata is untrusted; adapter validates against hub evidence references.

matrix.lossiness_note: Protocol content is not a provenance system. Adapter synthesizes canonical provenance from hub ledger state.
matrix.security_consequence: Loss of provenance prevents audit and accountability; must fail closed.
assumptions: Hub evidence store is the provenance authority.
matrix.owner_followup: S1-001 established the provenance evidence contract.

matrix.surface: knowledge proposal, promotion, challenge, rejection and revocation

mcp.native_field_selector: No knowledge status or promotion fields in MCP-2026-07-28-SPEC

a2a.native_field_selector: No knowledge status or promotion fields in A2A-1.0.0-SPEC

matrix.hub: Knowledge objects have status: proposal, verified, promoted, challenged, rejected, revoked, superseded. Promotion requires a separate canonical governance event. Protocol content is a proposal only.
matrix.hub_semantic: knowledge.status must be 'proposal' until a hub governance event promotes it. (Probe E)

adapter_mapping.MCP: Protocol tool output proposing/asserting knowledge -> status=proposal. No protocol payload can set promoted/verified. Silent promotion is forbidden. Loss of source digest/scope/challenge reference -> mapping rejected or status downgraded to proposal. (Probe E)
adapter_mapping.A2A: Same: protocol artifact content proposing knowledge -> status=proposal. Cannot self-promote.

matrix.lossiness_note: Knowledge promotion is absent from both protocols. Protocol content becomes a proposal only; promotion is hub-governance-only.
matrix.security_consequence: If protocol content could self-promote, it would bypass hub governance and epistemic controls.
assumptions: Knowledge governance is a hub-only decision surface.
matrix.owner_followup: S1-011 (knowledge gate) is the dedicated knowledge governance ticket.

mcp.native_field_selector: No revocation epoch or policy version binding in MCP base protocol; MCP Auth extension handles auth revocation at transport level (not policy version binding for effects).

a2a.native_field_selector: Agent Card has no policy version binding; auth revocation is at the connection/transport level in A2A-1.0.0-SPEC

matrix.hub: Policy version and revocation epoch are bound to every decision. A grant's revocation_epoch must be > the epoch at which it was issued.
matrix.hub_semantic: policy_version + revocation_epoch on every authorization decision; stale epoch -> DENY.

adapter_mapping.MCP: Adapter populates policy_version and revocation_epoch from hub policy ledger. Protocol payload cannot set or override these. Stale/fencing-miss -> DENY.
adapter_mapping.A2A: Same: hub policy ledger is the source. Protocol Task/agent card cannot set policy_version or revocation_epoch.

matrix.lossiness_note: Protocol has no policy version binding. Adapter injects from hub ledger only.
matrix.security_consequence: Revocation not binding on protocol tasks would allow revoked principals to continue operating.
assumptions: Hub policy ledger is the revocation authority.
matrix.owner_followup: S1-008 (revocation latency) defines the propagation bound.

mcp.native_field_selector: Capabilities field allows optional features; protocol_version in initialize negotiates version. Unknown extensions are implementation-specific in MCP-2026-07-28-SPEC

a2a.native_field_selector: Agent Card has 'capabilities' for optional features (streaming, pushNotifications); extensions are optional. Unknown capabilities are ignored by A2A-1.0.0-SPEC

matrix.hub: Extensions are accepted/rejected/quarantined with version provenance. Unknown version/extension -> quarantine/unsupported, never permissive default.
matrix.hub_semantic: extensions.accepted[], rejected[], quarantined[] with version provenance.

adapter_mapping.MCP: Unknown MCP extension or unsupported protocol_version -> QUARANTINED, not ignored. Adapter emits version evidence. Downgrade to an older permissive semantic -> REJECTED. (Probe F)
adapter_mapping.A2A: Unknown A2A capability or extension -> QUARANTINED. Adapter emits version evidence.

matrix.lossiness_note: Protocol has no host-side policy for unknown extensions. Adapter must quarantine rather than ignore.
matrix.security_consequence: Ignoring unknown extensions could allow an attacker to slip a malicious extension past the adapter.
assumptions: Adapter default is deny for unknown extensions.
matrix.owner_followup: S1-009 adapter contract defines extension quarantine rules.

mcp.native: MCP uses JSON-RPC 2.0 error objects with code and message. Tool errors return isError=true in CallToolResult. No formal terminal-state enumeration in MCP-2026-07-28-SPEC

a2a.native: A2A uses TaskState (COMPLETED, FAILED, CANCELLED, REJECTED, etc.) and JSON-RPC error objects. Terminal states are explicitly enumerated in A2A-1.0.0-SPEC
a2a.native_field_selector: TaskState terminal enum; JSON-RPC error via A2A-1.0.0-SPEC

matrix.hub: Errors map deterministically to hub terminal states. No protocol error/failure maps to a hub 'success' or 'acceptance'.
matrix.hub_semantic: protocol error -> hub error terminal (not success); protocol completion -> hub reconciliation (not terminal until verified).

adapter_mapping.MCP: MCP JSON-RPC error -> hub error event. MCP isError=true -> hub error. MCP success -> hub STATUS_REPORTED, not terminal; reconciliation continues.
adapter_mapping.A2A: A2A TaskState.FAILED/CANCELLED/REJECTED -> hub error/cancel event (fail-closed). A2A TaskState.COMPLETED -> hub STATUS_REPORTED, not terminal until reconciliation confirms.

matrix.lossiness_note: Protocol terminal states do not imply hub terminal states. Adapter must not map protocol completion to hub acceptance.
matrix.security_consequence: Mapping protocol completion to hub acceptance would allow protocol payloads to declare goals accepted.
assumptions: Hub terminal state is decided only by the hub state machine + reconciliation + Gate evaluation.
matrix.owner_followup: S1-009 adapter contract defines error/terminal-state mapping rules.

mcp.native_field_selector: No structured audit event or replay mechanism in MCP-2026-07-28-SPEC beyond request/response logging at the implementation level

a2a.native_field_selector: No structured audit event or replay mechanism in A2A-1.0.0-SPEC; Task history is client-side state, not an audit log

matrix.hub: Every state transition + audit event commits atomically. Events are replay-safe (idempotency keys). Audit events carry actor, operation, decision reason, and audit reference.
matrix.hub_semantic: journal: atomic transition + audit event commit; replay via idempotency key.

adapter_mapping.MCP: Adapter emits hub audit events for every protocol message translated. Protocol request/response logs are NOT audit events. Replay is hub-side via idempotency keys.
adapter_mapping.A2A: Same: adapter emits hub audit events. A2A Task history is untrusted input, not an audit log.

matrix.lossiness_note: Protocol lacks structured audit/replay. Adapter synthesizes hub audit events.
matrix.security_consequence: Without hub-side audit, delegation and budget changes would be unverifiable.
assumptions: Hub journal is the audit authority.

coverage_check.note: 12 rows pass lossless or lossy-safe mappings with documented security consequences; 3 rows (SM6 delegation, SM8 budget, SM11 knowledge promotion) are unsupported because the semantics are ABSENT from both protocols.
